run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The checkout service in namespace astronomy-shop is down because the Deployment checkout carries a nodeSelector (kubernetes.io/hostname=extra-node) that matches no node in the cluster: no node has the hostname label extra-node (nodes are sregym-control-plane, sregym-worker, sregym-worker2, sregym-worker3, the first being control-plane tainted), and the Deployment's pod template in both checkout ReplicaSets requires that selector. Both checkout pods are Pending with FailedScheduling '0/4 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: }, 3 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector', the Deployment reports Available=False / MinimumReplicasUnavailable, and the checkout Service has no endpoints. The last working checkout pod (checkout-6c769b88b5-2mw92, scheduled on sregym-worker) was stopped at 16:32:39 as part of a rollout to the new ReplicaSets, and the replacement pods can never schedule. As a consequence frontend's POST /api/checkout returns 500 with 'connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.81.128:8080' (10.96.81.128 is the checkout Service ClusterIP) and the load generator records failures only on POST /api/checkout while every other endpoint shows zero failures. checkout is the only deployment in the namespace with a nodeSelector, which isolates the fault to it. A second, so-far latent misconfiguration exists in the same pod template: PRODUCT_CATALOG_ADDR is product-catalog:8082 while product-catalog listens on 8080 (hypothesis, not yet observable because no checkout pod starts). The ad ServiceEndpointDown alert is a startup artifact, not a fault: its single probe sample (0 at 16:32:00) predates the ad container becoming ready at 16:32:07, and ad logs show it serving ad requests normally afterwards. Prometheus/Jaeger data in this environment begins only around 16:29-16:32, so no pre-incident baseline exists and the change history integration was not available, which is why who/what applied the nodeSelector cannot be established.

claims.text: Both checkout pods (checkout-54579c864c-rndwr and checkout-69887c97-258fm) are Pending with condition PodScheduled=False, reason Unschedulable, message '0/4 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: }, 3 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/4 nodes are available: 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'; each has spec.nodeSelector {"kubernetes.io/hostname":"extra-node"}.

The cluster has exactly four nodes with kubernetes.io/hostname labels sregym-control-plane (tainted node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane), sregym-worker, sregym-worker2 and sregym-worker3; no node carries the label value extra-node.

Deployment checkout (namespace astronomy-shop) has spec.template.spec.nodeSelector {"kubernetes.io/hostname":"extra-node"} and status conditions Available=False (reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable since 16:32:40) and Progressing=True (ReplicaSet checkout-c69887c97 is progressing), with replicas 2, unavailableReplicas 2, updatedReplicas 1.
checkout is the only Deployment in namespace astronomy-shop whose pod template has a nodeSelector; all 22 other deployments have nodeSelector null.

Both checkout ReplicaSets (checkout-54579c864c, revision 1, created 16:32:40, and checkout-c69887c97, revision 2, created 16:32:46) carry nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=extra-node and have no ready replicas.
Service checkout has selector opentelemetry.io/name=checkout and clusterIP 10.96.81.128, and its Endpoints object has an empty subsets list, i.e. no ready backend addresses.

The rollout sequence is visible in events: pod checkout-6c769b88b5-2mw92 was Scheduled to sregym-worker at 16:31:48, its checkout container Started at 16:32:20, was Stopping (reason Killing) at 16:32:39; the Deployment scaled up ReplicaSet checkout-54579c864c at 16:32:40 and ReplicaSet checkout-c69887c97 at 16:32:46, whose pods then hit FailedScheduling at 16:32:40 and 16:32:46.

frontend spans for POST /api/checkout carry status error=true, http.status_code=500, and its child oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder span carries rpc.grpc.status_code=14 with exception.message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.81.128:8080 (2026-11-21T16:32:51.814Z)'; 21 tcp.connect spans in the sample are also status ERROR with 'connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.81.128:8080'.

frontend pod logs repeat 'Error: 14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.81.128:8080' continuously from 16:32:08 to 16:32:51, whereas earlier refusals to 10.96.224.138:8080 (product-catalog), 10.96.12.164:3551 (product-reviews) and 10.96.211.146:8080 (ad) occur only around 16:31:59-16:32:05.

In the 5-minute window ending 16:32:57 the load generator recorded failures only on POST /api/checkout (increase(locust_requests_num_failures) = 3.54); all other endpoints (GET /, GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart, GET /api/products/*, GET /api/product-reviews/*, GET /api/recommendations*, POST /api/product-ask-ai-assistant/*) show 0.

Alerting rules loaded at 16:32:49 show ServiceEndpointDown pending for ad.astronomy-shop:8080 and checkout.astronomy-shop:8080, and HighRequestErrorRate pending for POST /api/checkout in astronomy-shop with value 1.00.

The live checkout pod template sets env PRODUCT_CATALOG_ADDR=product-catalog:8082, while the last-applied configuration recorded on the same Deployment had PRODUCT_CATALOG_ADDR=product-catalog:8080, and the product-catalog Deployment exposes containerPort 8080 with Service product-catalog port 8080.

At evaluation instant 16:32:57 probe_success is 1 for cart, currency, email, flagd, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, kafka, payment, product-catalog, product-reviews, quote, recommendation and shipping endpoints, and 0 only for ad.astronomy-shop:8080 and checkout.astronomy-shop:8080.

The unschedulable checkout pods and the resulting empty checkout Endpoints are caused by the nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=extra-node in the checkout Deployment pod template, which no node in this cluster satisfies; the mechanism is fully consistent between the FailedScheduling message, the live node labels and the empty Endpoints. What applied that selector is unknown (no change history available).

A second, currently latent misconfiguration is the checkout template's PRODUCT_CATALOG_ADDR=product-catalog:8082: once a checkout pod schedules it would call the product-catalog Service on port 8082 while that Service and container listen on 8080, which would break checkout's GetProduct calls. No impact from it is observed yet because no checkout pod has started.

The ad ServiceEndpointDown alert and probe_success=0 for ad.astronomy-shop:8080 are not an ad-service fault: the only probe sample in 16:00-16:32:57 is 0 at 16:32:00, while the ad container logged 'Ad service started, listening on 8080' at 16:32:09 and then served targeted ad requests at 16:32:13, 16:32:17, 16:32:24, 16:32:29, 16:32:34, 16:32:44 and 16:32:50 with no error lines.

No flagd fault-injection flag is switched on in ConfigMap flagd-config: every flag listed (llmInaccurateResponse, llmRateLimitError, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad, failedReadinessProbe, emailMemoryLeak) has defaultVariant 'off'.

A dependency of checkout (cart, currency, payment, email, shipping, product-catalog, kafka or flagd) is the failing component: those deployments report 1 available replica, their blackbox probes read 1 at 16:32:57, their Endpoints have addresses, and checkout's failure is a connection refused at the checkout Service IP before any downstream call is made (the child CheckoutService/PlaceOrder span fails with grpc status 14 and no downstream checkout spans exist).

The observability/other startup churn in the window (Killing of otel-collector-agent-4p4kl/5q2lg/lwk6c, Unhealthy probes on otel-collector-agent-56ns8/5q2lg, opensearch-0 and grafana-7b9cbf56f5-7xc5d at 16:31:49-16:32:31) is not the cause of the checkout failure: those events coincide with the monitoring stack and opensearch starting, and none of them touches the checkout pods, Service or Endpoints.

Remove or correct the checkout Deployment's spec.template.spec.nodeSelector (kubernetes.io/hostname=extra-node) so pods can schedule on sregym-worker/-worker2/-worker3, and in the same change restore PRODUCT_CATALOG_ADDR to product-catalog:8080; then verify that both checkout pods become Ready, the checkout Endpoints object gains an address, and POST /api/checkout returns 200 with zero locust failures.

gaps: The change-history integration is not available in this Run, so who or what added nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=extra-node to checkout and at exactly which time cannot be established; the Deployment's own creationTimestamp is 16:31:48 and its last-applied-configuration already contains the selector, so the patch method, patch time and actor are unknown.

No pre-incident baseline exists: Prometheus series for probe_success (blackbox-astronomy-shop) and traces_span_metrics_calls_total only have samples in the last seconds of the window (first sample seen at 16:32:00 and 16:32:57 respectively) and Jaeger's earliest returned spans start at 16:31:49, so I cannot state how long checkout had been failing or compare latency/error rates against a baseline.

Rate-based error/latency aggregations over traces_span_metrics_calls_total (sum by service_name of rate/increase with status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR over 2m and 5m) returned no data at 16:32:57 even though the raw series returned samples, so per-service error rates could not be computed; error evidence therefore rests on Jaeger spans, frontend logs and locust metrics.

Runtime flagd flag state cannot be verified (no flagd/OFREP query tool and flagd-config holds only default variants, all off); an override published at runtime through the flagd UI/OFREP endpoint would not be visible in this evidence.

kube_deployment_status_replicas_available for checkout still reads 1 at 16:32:57 while the Deployment object records Available=False since 16:32:40 and has no ready pod; this inconsistency (likely scrape/aggregation lag) is unresolved and that series was not used to judge checkout availability.

No NetworkPolicy objects were returned by the query for namespace astronomy-shop (status no_data, empty result), so I cannot state whether traffic policies exist; this empty result is not evidence that none exist.

Logs of the terminated pod checkout-6c769b88b5-2mw92 (the last checkout instance that did run) are not retrievable because the pod was deleted; whether it logged errors before it was stopped at 16:32:39 is unknown.
The single-sample probe_success=0 for ad cannot be compared to earlier samples, so ad's probe history before 16:32:00 is unknown.
next_steps: Inspect the Deployment checkout rollout history/audit log (change history) to identify what applied nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=extra-node at 16:32:40 and PRODUCT_CATALOG_ADDR=product-catalog:8082 at 16:32:46.
If a node named extra-node is genuinely intended, provision/label that node (or remove the selector from the checkout pod template) and confirm scheduling.
After checkout becomes Ready, validate checkout's calls to product-catalog on port 8080 rather than 8082 and watch for GetProduct failures.
Confirm whether any flagd flag was published at runtime through the flagd UI/OFREP endpoint, since the ConfigMap alone shows all defaults off.
